question.prompt:
Let \(ABC\) be an equilateral triangle. Extend side \(\overline{AB}\) beyond \(B\) to a point \(B'\) so that \(BB'=3 \cdot AB.\) Similarly, extend side \(\overline{BC}\) beyond \(C\) to a point \(C'\) so that \(CC'=3 \cdot BC,\) and extend side \(\overline{CA}\) beyond \(A\) to a point \(A'\) so that \(AA'=3 \cdot CA.\)

What is the ratio of the area of \(\triangle A'B'C'\) to the area of \(\triangle ABC?\)

solutions.title: Add areas with shared heights
solutions.explanation:
The useful observation is that triangles with bases on the same line and the same opposite vertex have equal heights, so their areas are proportional to their bases.

Write \([PQR]\) for the area of \(\triangle PQR\), and let \(X=[ABC]\). Consider the subdivision obtained by joining \(C\) to \(B'\), \(A\) to \(C'\), and \(B\) to \(A'\), together with the original triangle's sides.

Triangles \(BB'C\) and \(ABC\) have bases \(BB'\) and \(AB\) on the same line and share vertex \(C\). Since \(BB'=3AB\), we get \([BB'C]=3X\). Applying the same comparison on the other two extended sides gives
\[
[BB'C]=[CC'A]=[AA'B]=3X.
\]

Now compare \(AA'C'\) with \(ACC'\). Their bases \(AA'\) and \(AC\) lie on the same line, their opposite vertex is \(C'\), and \(AA'=3AC\). Hence
\[
[AA'C']=3[ACC']=9X.
\]
The corresponding comparisons at the other corners give
\[
[CC'B']=3[BCB']=9X,
\qquad
[BB'A']=3[ABA']=9X.
\]

The subdivision fills the outer triangle without overlapping interiors: it consists of \(ABC\), the three triangles of area \(3X\), and the three corner triangles of area \(9X\). Therefore
\[
[A'B'C']=X+3(3X)+3(9X)=37X.
\]
The requested ratio is \(\boxed{37:1}\), choice E.

solutions.title: Congruence and a general cosine-law side ratio
